Title: Want to fix Weenies, then fix tapping to block

Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:
One of the main design flaws with VTES is that small cap vampires are
better than large cap vampires.

The reason for this is that you have to tap when you block. So
basically if you have more minions you will tap out all the blockers.

What if the rule was changed so that when blocking you only tapped if
the vampire was the same age or older. You wouldn't tap for smaller
vampires and you wouldn't tap for allies.

What do you think?

I think it is a sound idea, but :

a) it solves part of the "situation", because weenies will be able to make
actions that pass (with natural or added stealth, or rush actions that cost
you a minion if he blocks, etc.), so really it adresses only the issue of
the mass non-stealthed bleed decks, which aren't that numerous.

b) not tapping for allies would be harsh against many, many allies
(especially seeing as even a Tumninos wouldn't tap when blocking, say, 2
Nocturns...)

c) a big part of the "problem" is that a 3-Cap with the right discipline or
equipment or both can send to torpor a 10-cap without much imaginative
effort.

I really think that it is too late now to address this in the global design
of things.

My take in adapting the RPG would have been cards with levels of power, and
you can play only a level equal or inferior to your capacity. But of course
it's way too late for that.

So we just have to trust the designers to compensate that "flaw" as well as
they can...

Orpheus

Messages.Author: quickbeam
Messages.Body:
On Feb 13, 4:09 pm, XZealot <xzea...@cox.net> wrote:



I think such a rule change is a bad idea. It would completely change
the fabric of the game. I also think that weenies are better for
other reasons, such as the fact that all vampires have a default bleed
of 1, so your ratio of resources to potential offense is lower with
weenies. Blocking is part of the picture, but not the main part.

Second, life has been getting easier for mid caps and large caps
incrementally. Target Vitals makes things harder for weenies.
Tension, Dragonbound, Neonate Breech, and Anarchist Uprising turn them
into liabilities. Sense the Savage Way and Forced March have improved
things for mid and large caps. Banning PTO was a huge help. In my
opinion, Pentex is the last real problem card that benefits weenies to
the detriment of the game. It is becoming an automatic include for
competitive decks, which is boring and bad for the game.

The level of opportunistic combat which kills little minions keeps
rising, and I think that is a better way to keep weenies in check than
turning over the whole apple cart in the street. Changing a core rule
like who needs to tap to block who seems incredibly disruptive to the
game, and unwarranted.

-dc

I think:

1) You might have had a fair argument about weenies eight or ten
years ago. I don't find them to be more than just one archetypal
choice now - and one with distinct weaknesses as well as strengths.

2) Library cards and vampires have been designed around the blocking
rule as written for many years. Changing it so drastically now would
screw up the balance of the game.

I'm really surprised anyone is still complaining about weenies.
If the game has a flaw, it's more along the lines that some of
the biggest vampires in the game don't have enough advantages to
merit the cost of influencing them in. But then again, many
actually do - so even that one's not such a horrible problem.

Fred

Messages.Author: Kevin M.
Messages.Body:
Peter D Bakija wrote:
> Not that I think that Norm's initial suggestion needs implementing
> (the short version is that there have been *plenty* of cards
> introduced into the game recently that power up mongo vampires
> and power down weenies, so I think the balance scale is getting
> a lot closer to balanced than it used to be),

[snip]

While I agree with what you said above, the issue is that if you are
playing large-cap vampires with these cards with the argument that
you need them to balance out the small-cap advantage, you are being
forced by the nature of large- and small-cap vampires to spend
valuable card slots on cards which could instead be partially
implemented by some kind of rules addition.

For example, my personal dream-world rules change would be to reprint
Freak Drive to be once per turn and then to implement a rule stating
that vampires with capacity 8 or above may burn 1 blood to untap once
during their minion phase.

Clearly, small-cap vampires have an action-advantage that large-cap
vampires have no base defense against. Large-cap vampires have no
consistent bleed advantage, no consistent strength-advantage,
no consistent intercept advantage, and a clear pool disadvantage.
The only thing they really have going for them is that once you get
them out you have more options. If you survive.



Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija

On Feb 14, 2:15 pm, "Kevin M." <youw...@imaspammer.org> wrote:
> While I agree with what you said above, the issue is that if you are
> playing large-cap vampires with these cards with the argument that
> you need them to balance out the small-cap advantage, you are being
> forced by the nature of large- and small-cap vampires to spend

> implemented by some kind of rules addition.

Well, they could be, sure, but big vampires have a lot of advantages
in and of themselves (lots of options, votes, special abilities). I
mean, don't get me wrong here--there is certainly a very concrete
advantage to weenies over big guys (i.e. 10 pool spent on 1 guy is
much less effective, generally speaking, than 10 pool spent on 10
guys). And most of the cards that upgrade the big guys aren't just
narrow weenie hosers (i.e. I'm not thinking about Minor Irritation
here :-); they tend to be strong in and of themselves--Enkil Cog,
Sense the Savage Way, and Neonate Breach, for example, are good just
to play all the time, not just when you expect weenies. And in recent
history, big vampires have gotten a lot of very solid special
abilities, making them a lot more worth the effort.

> For example, my personal dream-world rules change would be to reprint
> Freak Drive to be once per turn and then to implement a rule stating
> that vampires with capacity 8 or above may burn 1 blood to untap once
> during their minion phase.

Well, yeah, Freak Drive certainly needs to be once per turn :-)

I don't know that 8+ caps need to be able to free freak drive,
however. Especially given the growing number of cards that do that for
you anyway, and work better when you are large as opposed to small
(Monster and Cavalier for example).

> Clearly, small-cap vampires have an action-advantage that large-cap
> vampires have no base defense against.  Large-cap vampires have no
> consistent bleed advantage, no consistent strength-advantage,
> no consistent intercept advantage, and a clear pool disadvantage.

All of this is very true. But still, recent additions to the game have
gone a long way towards evening things up. I see *way* more big
vampire decks doing well consistently these days than I did back in
the day.

-Peter

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:

> Still, mono inferior dominate has next to no combat defense except
> discipline-less Fake Out, Dodge, and maybe Thoughts Betrayed if you're

(Absorb the Mind--dom Dodge).

Sure. It isn't, like, the best deck in the world or anything, but
weenie mono discipline decks (Dom/Pre/Dem) tend to be incredibly fast,
incredibly debilitating, and bleed for 4-5 an action. And while they
don't show up constantly (mostly out of fear of physical abuse :-),
they still show up. And do pretty well. They aren't going to sweep
every table, no, but they are going to sweep some tables.

>  More importantly, spending one blood on the Govern
> and one on the Conditioning is impossible for a one cap and can't get
> done twice in a row only by two and three caps.  So, still, you don't
> really see these decks in practice so my answer is the same: not a
> problem.

Weenie Presence still sees play all the time. Bleeding for 3-5 per
action with 2-3 caps is not at all uncommon. Same with weenie
Dementation. Jackie and Midget bleed for 4 per action. At stealth
even. Without spending any blood at all. And are 3 caps. Weenie Dom is
certainly not the most optimal of the weenie bleedzookas due to the
blood costs, but you get out a 3 cap, bleed your prey for 5, and then
next turn, play Life in the City and do it again. You get this through
4 times, their game is done. And that isn't that hard to do.

I mean, yeah, again, I don't think this justifies making up a new rule
so that big guys don't tap when blocking little guys. But it is not at
all out of the realm of reason to think that 3 caps bleeding for 4-5
per action is not that uncommon. Which goes back to the old "VTES
Reset" plan that has been around for a hundred years now, where cards
are modified/removed such that it is hard (if not impossible) to bleed
for more than 3 with an inferior discipline.

> *bang!*  Heh!

I certainly need to strongly consider if I want to put this together
in reality and take for a spin. Someone will punch me :-)

-Peter

the game, I think the balance is a lot closer to even now. I mean,
yeah, still, if a Saulot deck sits in front of a weenie pre bleed
deck, it is going to get wiped out before it does anything cool. But
that is likely true of most decks in that position.

Ah, how 'bout that. There _is_ a free Dom dodge...

> Sure. It isn't, like, the best deck in the world or anything, but
> weenie mono discipline decks (Dom/Pre/Dem) tend to be incredibly fast,
> incredibly debilitating, and bleed for 4-5 an action. And while they
> don't show up constantly (mostly out of fear of physical abuse :-),
> they still show up. And do pretty well. They aren't going to sweep
> every table, no, but they are going to sweep some tables.
>
> > More importantly, spending one blood on the Govern

>
> Weenie Presence still sees play all the time. Bleeding for 3-5 per
> action with 2-3 caps is not at all uncommon.

I have actually never seen the dom weeny deck myself in a tournament.
I've seen people play presence weenie from time to time. I'm pretty
sure the difference is the availability of S:CE, which is a whole lot
harder chew through for a combat deck. That is, you may get a couple
guys in a hurry - but most combat decks will run through a lot of
combat cards torping or burning minions from a deck with a fair amount
of S:CE. I suspect the usual pattern is to run out of combat cards
trying to do so.

And inferior presense bleed for 5 has the same problem as the
inferior dominate bleed for 5: the bleed card costs a blood and the
bleed modifier costs a blood, meaning a 2 or 3 cap vampire is not
going to do this twice in a row. In fact, unless you're Toreador, I'm
not sure how to do a bleed for 5. You bleed for four every third
turn. Even so, it's better than dom due to the S:CE thing. IMHO.

> Same with weenie
> Dementation. Jackie and Midget bleed for 4 per action. At stealth
> even. Without spending any blood at all. And are 3 caps.

Not sure who Jackie is. But you know the problem with Midget as you
type that: you spend pool to make Midget act - that's worse than
spending the blood.

> Weenie Dom is
> certainly not the most optimal of the weenie bleedzookas due to the
> blood costs, but you get out a 3 cap, bleed your prey for 5, and then
> next turn, play Life in the City and do it again. You get this through
> 4 times, their game is done. And that isn't that hard to do.

Well, actually, I'd dispute that it isn't hard to do. It looks pretty
dicey to get four of them off to me, given their defenselessness and
the blood they spend to do it even once.

> I mean, yeah, again, I don't think this justifies making up a new rule
> so that big guys don't tap when blocking little guys. But it is not at
> all out of the realm of reason to think that 3 caps bleeding for 4-5
> per action is not that uncommon.

In the places I play, it seems to be - and most likely for the drawbacks
I've cited.

Fred

I suppose. Except that the major formula for getting those bleeds
through is by outnumbering the other guys on a given turn - which
is hard to do if you get snot kicked out of the first guys who run
into blockers the first turn you do it. Yea, you can get the extra
bleed or two in early sometimes. And you can probably refill the
odd pool on some guys with LitC or with a bit of Blood Doll push.
But trying to keep enough guys on the board to get your stealthless
bleeds through gets very hard very fast, especially if someone draws
a mittful of Wakes early and got some combat to go with it. And
even if it works on the first prey, I usually see the whole thing
come to a grinding halt on the second prey, who's both had plenty
of time to setup and very little pressure on him at all after the
first prey stopped all forward motion once he realized who he was
dealing with. Even weenie presense often suffers this fate. Weenie
dominate would need a hell of a lot table luck to avoid it, I think.

> > Not sure who Jackie is. But you know the problem with Midget as you
> > type that: you spend pool to make Midget act - that's worse than
> > spending the blood.
>
> Jackie is the 3 cap DEM (G4).

Ah, yes. She's the Keith Moody of Dem. Sure, there's one.

> I'm gathering that you don't see much
> weenie Dementation around your parts either. It is really good.

Weenie Dem is something different. Dementation has its own stealth.
Usually, though, I think people just take a look at the Dementation
cards that are out there and reason that the solution to 5-6 cap
Dementation is the same solution as to weenie Dementation but the
midcap stuff delivers the bleed much more reliably. Why bother
sending weenies to get blocked and maybe torped when you can just
waltz right past the blockers with _all_ your minions given a half
decent draw? I think the point of both weenie Dem and weenie Dom
is pretty hard to justify. The point of weenie presence, on the
other hand, makes a lot more sense in that your initial bleeders
who get blocked, often will survive with S:CE. (Plus there's
probably fewer good presence/obfuscate bleeders than dom/obf or
dem/obf.)

> I mean, yeah, you only bleed for 4 per action instead of 5, but
> you also get the stealth. And to gain a pool. Midget, infernal
> and all, is total gold in this sort of situation.

I say use Jackie and Midget with Persia, Uncle George, and Apache
Jones.

Hmmm. Maybe _I'll_ build that deck - just to be a pain.

> > Well, actually, I'd dispute that it isn't hard to do. It looks pretty
> > dicey to get four of them off to me, given their defenselessness and
> > the blood they spend to do it even once.
>
> You bleed for 5 on T2 before your prey gets out a minion. Next turn,
> you tap their minion with Misdirection and bleed for 5 twice. I mean,
> not always going to happen. But not at all an unreasonable thing to
> consider.

...and then often you'll draw that misdirection after your 1st 10
cards or so - when it won't do a lot of good. Personally, I like
Anarch Troublemakers for this purpose instead of Misdirections.
It's free, will tap two minions, and it keeps going around the
table, which means you may get to use it again later (after all,
you plan on tapping out all the time anyway) or you may get to
contest it with your prey, which is cool either way. An Anarch
Troublemaker, drawn at a bad time, can be laid down on the table,
removed from the hand free of charge, and saved until a good time
to set off.

The one drawback is the turn of delay and advanced warning your
predator gets. The former is unfortunate but still not a bad tradeoff
for the card's benefits and the latter isn't that important.

> > In the places I play, it seems to be - and most likely for the drawbacks
> > I've cited.
>
> Weenies bleeding for 4-5 per action is rare, or weenie dominate is
> rare?

Both. (That is to say, both are rare.) I don't recall seeing a weenie
domainate deck in a tournament. (But, of course, I have CRS - it's a
terrible disease and it means you can't totally trust me on this.)

Fred
